# Loom 4.0 in CI

Use `loom build PROJECT` to compile a project in CI. The examples use a project directory named `widget`. This guide covers the compiler-version policy, the remote object cache switches, and the small set of cache diagnostics discussed here. The configuration details in this guide are intended to help with the configuration work involved in setting up these options for CI.

## Choose the job policy

CI jobs MUST pin the exact compiler version. This is a requirement on the compiler used by the job. CI jobs SHOULD use the remote object cache when it is reachable. The cache recommendation does not make cache use a requirement: compiling without that cache is supported.

Keep the strength of these two statements separate when writing job templates. The version pin is mandatory. Remote cache use is recommended under the stated reachability condition. An uncached build does not become unsupported merely because the recommendation favors a reachable cache.

## Control reads and writes

Default cache policy permits reads from the remote object cache. It also permits writes to that cache. Two negative flags change different parts of this policy:

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--no-cache` | Disables cache reads; it does not disable cache writes. |
| `--no-store` | Disables cache writes; it does not disable cache reads. |

With a reachable cache and `--no-cache` alone, a build may send newly compiled objects to the cache but will not read reusable objects from it. With a reachable cache and `--no-store` alone, a build may read reusable objects but will not send new objects from that build. Combining the two flags disables both operations.

The names of the flags can look like broad ways to turn caching off. Their scope is narrower: one changes read permission, and the other changes write permission. When choosing a command, identify the operation you want to disable.

## Interpret the output

The lookup identifier field is `cache_key`. It identifies a compiler-input fingerprint, not a filesystem path. The lookup result field is `hit`. A true value means a cached object was retrieved; it does not establish that the linked executable is byte-identical to a prior executable.

```json
{"cache_key":"fp_91","hit":true}
```

This output reports an object retrieved using fingerprint identifier `fp_91`. Interpret the result at the object-cache level. The meaning of the hit field does not expand to a comparison of complete linked executables.

## Bound slot waiting

The cache-slot wait option is `--wait-ms`. Its value is an integer number of milliseconds spent waiting to acquire a cache connection slot. It is not a compilation-duration limit. The accepted range is 0 through 60000 inclusive. Zero requests no waiting for a slot. The value 60000 is valid; 60001 is invalid.

For example:

```sh
loom build widget --no-cache --wait-ms 250
loom build widget --no-store --wait-ms 250
```

Both commands allow up to 250 milliseconds to acquire a cache connection slot. The first permits writes but not reads. The second permits reads but not writes. Their equal waiting limits do not make their cache policies equivalent.
